summary: payment-service's mTLS client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z without renewal. From 12:15:27Z every bank-partner-api call fails with 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)', bank_api_error_rate goes to 100% and payment_success_rate collapses to ~2%, matching ~40 customer tickets about failed transfers. The HTTP error-rate panel stayed green (~0.2%) because affected payments are marked PENDING_RETRY rather than returned as 5xx, so the symptom was invisible on the standard error dashboard. Category: credential_expiry. Fix is to issue/install a renewed client certificate and re-process PENDING_RETRY payments; add renewal automation (same failure mode as historical HIST-106).

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service mTLS client certificate expired, breaking bank-partner-api calls
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal used by payment-service to authenticate to bank-partner-api expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z and was not renewed. All bank-partner-api calls then fail at the TLS handshake, payments cannot be submitted to the bank, and payments are marked PENDING_RETRY instead of returning errors, so the HTTP error-rate panel stays green while real payment success collapses to ~2%.

causal_chain.claim: client cert notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z (cert-watcher warned 25 min earlier)
cert expires -> mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected from 12:15:27Z
bank_api_error_rate goes to 100% and payment_success_rate to ~2%
payments marked PENDING_RETRY instead of HTTP 5xx -> error_rate panel stays ~0.2%

assumptions: The CN=payment cert expiry timestamp in logs is the actual applied credential (not a stale config reference).
No renewed cert was deployed between 12:15Z and 13:59Z (error logs continue to the latest data).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bank partner API outage on the vendor side (dependency_failure)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The bank partner's API is down/returning errors, causing our bank calls to fail, as in historical incident HIST-105.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Error text explicitly says 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert ... notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' and cert-watcher flagged our own cert expiring at exactly 12:15:00Z. The fault is our credential, not the partner's availability.

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service config change (bank.api.timeout_ms 3s->5s) caused failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-2502 raising the bank API timeout to 5000ms caused payment failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The config change was 55 minutes before onset, changed only a timeout, and latency actually DECREASED (~320ms->140ms) post-onset; failures are TLS handshake errors tied to cert notAfter=12:15:00Z.

ranked_hypotheses.title: settlement-service v1.9.0 deploy broke payment flow
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 10:30Z settlement-service deployment (CSV exporter) introduced a fault that surfaces in payments.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: settlement-service shows no error logs; onset 12:15Z coincides exactly with the payment cert expiry, not the 10:30Z deploy.

facts.statement: payment-service's client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal had notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z and triggered a cert-watcher warning 25 minutes prior.
mTLS handshakes with bank-partner-api were rejected from 12:15:27Z and continued through the latest data (13:58Z).
bank_api_error_rate rose from ~0.2% to 75% then 100%; payment_success_rate fell from ~99% to ~2.5%.
The HTTP error_rate metric stayed flat at ~0.22% mean throughout, so the standard dashboard was green.
Only config change was cfg-2502 (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 11:20Z) and only deployment was settlement-service dep-5510 at 10:30Z; neither aligns with the 12:15Z onset.
bank-partner-api is external with no telemetry, and the error text attributes failure to our own client cert, not partner availability.

assumptions: The logged notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z reflects the actual in-use credential, not a stale config reference.
PENDING_RETRY payments are recoverable via retry after cert renewal (not permanently dropped).

recommended_actions.action: Issue and install a renewed client certificate for CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal (or roll a valid one) and confirm bank-partner-api mTLS handshakes succeed again.
recommended_actions.rationale: The expired cert (notAfter 12:15:00Z) is the direct cause of 100% bank_api_error_rate and ~2% payment success.

recommended_actions.action: Reprocess/retry the payments accumulated in PENDING_RETRY once mTLS is restored.
recommended_actions.rationale: Payments were deferred rather than lost; customers need the transfers completed.

recommended_actions.action: Add an alert on bank_api_error_rate / payment_success_rate and on cert expiry lead time (not just HTTP error_rate), since the standard 5xx panel stayed green.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failure was invisible on the HTTP error-rate dashboard; PENDING_RETRY masking makes this a recurring blind spot.

recommended_actions.action: Automate certificate renewal/rotation with proactive expiry alerting for all services.
recommended_actions.rationale: Matches root cause of historical incident HIST-106 ('no renewal automation'); prevents recurrence.

data_gaps: No telemetry for bank-partner-api (has_telemetry=false); could not directly confirm partner-side health, though error text attributes failure to our client cert.
No certificate-management/secret-store tool was available to confirm whether a renewal was attempted or failed between 12:15Z and 13:59Z.
Log results were truncated (truncated=true) in several queries; counts are lower bounds but the dominant patterns are consistent across queries.

findings.statement: bank_api_error_rate for payment-service jumps from ~0.2% (through 12:00Z) to avg 75.05% at the 12:12Z bucket and then flat 100% from 12:24Z onward.
payment_success_rate for payment-service collapses from ~99% before 12:12Z to avg 26.82% at 12:12Z and ~2.5% thereafter, confirming customers' payments are broadly failing.
The HTTP error_rate metric stayed flat at ~0.2% throughout the incident (avg 0.22, max 0.32), explaining why the error-rate dashboard looked green despite mass payment failures.
payment-service latency_p99 dropped from ~320ms to ~140ms after 12:12Z, consistent with bank calls failing fast at the TLS handshake rather than hanging.
The only config change in the window is cfg-2502 on payment-service: bank.api.timeout_ms raised 3000->5000 at 11:20:00Z, before the 12:15Z cert expiry.
Only one deployment occurred in the window: settlement-service v1.9.0 (dep-5510, 'Batch settlement report export') at 10:30Z; no payment-service deployment.
bank-partner-api is an external node with has_telemetry=false; no partner-side telemetry is available, but the error text attributes the failure to our client cert.

Historical incident HIST-106 (2025-06-30, settlement-service) was 'Settlement mTLS certificate expired' with root cause 'Client certificate expired; no renewal automation', category credential_expiry.

refs.quote: Client certificate expired; no renewal automation

findings.statement: settlement-service shows no error-level logs in the window (only 5 WARNs: GC pauses, one connection reset, NTP drift), so the settlement deploy is not producing failures.

Inference: affected payments are marked PENDING_RETRY rather than returned as HTTP 5xx, so the client-facing HTTP status stays 200 and only the bank_api_error_rate/payment_success_rate metrics reveal the failure.
